proposals.relationship: Erickson compares Clark’s three forms of household production with the family economy categories used jointly by Louise Tilly and Joan Scott.
proposals.evidence_note: Erickson’s 1992 introduction ix explicitly aligns Clark’s domestic, family and capitalistic industry with Tilly and Scott’s 1978 family economy, family wage economy and family consumer economy terminology. The comparison is the named scholar’s account, not proof of direct transmission or identical chronology. Louise Tilly’s equal credit is retained; she has no full endpoint and is distinct from Charles Tilly. Erickson immediately questions Clark’s chronology and the conflation of capitalism with mechanization. Clark’s own introduction 6–8 says the forms overlap and coexist rather than succeeding along hard boundaries. Original Tilly–Scott 1978 book and the complete Clark book remain unread.
